title: Only the text while reading
statement: While students read, show only the text; bring questions only after the reading, take reading help away once a question appears, and let students look back at the text anytime.
detail: A content review of a reference reading lesson asked for only the story on screen while reading, the question after the timer or read-aloud ends, the reading guide's commentary gone once a quick-check question appears, since it scaffolds the text and not the question, and a back button while reading, since free movement is what a screen loses against a book (`grade3-reading/artifacts/feedback-aladdin-2026-08-25/feedback-text.txt`, lines 6-7). The course encoded each as a criterion, and its register lists them as met in the renderer (`grade3-reading/artifacts/criteria-register.csv`, lines 110-112). Let the student go back at any time while reading.
against: An earlier review's repair list asked to "rebuild reading purpose" (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/HOTBUCKET.md`, line 92), so a reading purpose is still wanted somewhere. A later run found: For one modelling routine the Grade 3 procedure spec plans the opposite: the learner never goes back to earlier parts' text, and the lesson gives a plain description of the first part with at most one carried quote, quoting only the current part on screen (`grade3-reading/course-renderer/docs/pedagogy/modelling-moment-procedures.md`, line 866) (`grade3-reading/course-renderer/docs/pedagogy/modelling-moment-procedures.md`). A later run found counter-evidence (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/skills/g3-reading-red-team/references/dimensions/D3-reading-architecture.md`).

A passage page offers back every EARLIER part of its story, never a later one (`readingsBefore` in `derive-layout.ts`, rendered by `PassageNode`). A story arrives one part per page and the child's only control is Next, so by part two part one is gone: holding it in their head while answering about part two is the split-attention cost the split layout exists to remove.

the child never goes back to earlier parts' text. Step 2's THEN evidence = a plain description of Part 1 plus at most one carried quote from the continuity brief; only the current part's text is quoted on screen.
Keep all previously unlocked text accessible. Gating forward is fine; nothing may lock behind the student.

Regressions in reading are genuine re-reading rather than memory checks (Booth & Weger, 2013), and a trailing mask that allowed forward reading but blocked regressions measurably impaired comprehension — not only on ambiguous sentences (Schotter, Tran & Rayner, 2014).
Give the audio per-section replay and scrub-back, so the reading is as re-hearable as the text is re-readable.
This is the strongest evidence cited in this document, and it moves backward locking from a preference to a defect.
Schotter, Tran & Rayner (2014) used a trailing mask that permitted forward reading but blocked regressions and found measurably impaired comprehension, not only on ambiguous sentences.
Locking backward removes re-reading, and re-reading is how comprehension gets repaired.
Questions come after reading, not during it.
read first, undistracted; then the active part
